items.note: APPEARANCE FIX, no action: the two shells 0.10.2's one-focus-ring-per-field pass missed. A focused ds-input or ds-textarea drew TWO rings - the 4px control ring the universal :where(:focus-visible) rule puts on the inner input/textarea, plus the 3px field halo the box paints on :focus-within. The inner one is now suppressed. ACTION only if you wrote a workaround: a rule that killed one of the two (box-shadow: none on an inner input, a re-declared --ds-input-focus-shadow meant to hide the doubling) can go. Deliberately NOT suppressed: the clear button and the password toggle inside the same box keep their own ring, because both are real tab stops the box halo cannot distinguish.
items.verify: Tab into a ds-input and a ds-textarea: each shows exactly one ring, the halo around the box. Tab on to the clear button or password toggle inside that field and a second, tighter ring appears on the button - that one is intended.

items.note: ACCESSIBILITY FIX, no action: 0.10.2's ring fix silenced the base focus indicator with a shell-wide reset, which also hit .search-clear - a tabindex=0 tab stop. Tabbing from the input to the clear button changed nothing on screen (box-shadow, outline, border, background and colour all identical), so a keyboard user could not tell the button had focus: a WCAG 2.4.7 failure. Every shell now names the single control it silences, so tab stops inside a field box keep their own ring. ACTION only if you re-added a ring to that button yourself - that rule can go.
items.verify: Type into a ds-search so the clear button appears, then Tab: the × shows its own ring on top of the field halo. Same for a chip close button in ds-autocomplete or ds-multi-select, and for the arrows in ds-number-stepper.

informational: The shell list in styles/_focus.scss is now maintained from a measurement, not from a read of the code: it had been wrong for two releases. If you add a component that paints its own ring on :focus-within, suppress the base rule on the control it speaks for - `outline: 0` cannot do it, because the base indicator is a box-shadow.

Two authoring mixins are now documented for consumers building their own composite controls: `focus.owns-the-focus-ring($control)` in styles/focus, and `text-clip.single-line-ellipsis` in styles/text-clip. Both are opt-in - no existing code changes.

deleteList.why: A rule killing one of the two focus rings a ds-input or ds-textarea used to paint - typically box-shadow: none on the inner input, or --ds-input-focus-shadow re-declared as none to hide the doubling.
deleteList.replaceWith: nothing - the component now paints one ring on its own
